description.narrative: 4. Implementing strategy 4.1 Intervention Approach, Methodology and Instruments The NGO Forum on Cambodia (NGOF) will implement theproject using a capacity strengthening, partnership, and evidence-based governance approach that promotes meaningful citizen participation in local planning and public financial management. The intervention adopts a rights-based and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) approach to ensure that women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, and LGBT communities actively participate in localgovernance and decision-making. The intervention is fully aligned with Cambodia's decentralisation reforms, particularly the National Programme for Sub-National Democratic Development (NP-SNDD II), the Commune Development Plan (CDP), Commune Investment Plan (CIP), District Integration Plan (DIP), and the Social Accountability Framework (ISAF). NGOF will deliver the intervention through four complementary strategies: 4.1.1 Capacity Development NGOF will strengthen the knowledge and skills of district councillors, communityrepresentatives, youth, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, LGBT groups, and civil society organisations on fiscal decentralisation, participatory planning, citizen engagement, and public financial management. The project will develop training curricula jointly with the National School of Local Administration (NASLA) and conduct capacity-building, coaching, and mentoring activitiesto strengthen both citizens and sub-national administrations. 4.1.2 Participatory Governance and Multi-stakeholder Dialogue The project will establish dialogue platforms with clear guidelines that bring together district administrations, commune councils, civil society organisations, community representatives, media, and relevant government institutions to jointly discuss local planning, budgeting, public expenditure, and service delivery. These platforms will strengthen trust, accountability, and collaborative problem-solving. 4.1.3 Evidence-based Learning and Policy Engagement NGOF will document lessons learned, collect evidence from local implementation, and produce policy recommendations that contribute to improving citizen participation and local public financial management. Evidence generated through district-level implementation will support national dialogue and policy improvement. 4.1.4 Institutional Partnership Rather than creating parallel systems, NGOF will work through existing government structures and collaborate closely with NASLA, district administrations, commune councils, civil society networks, and community groups to institutionalise participatory governance within Cambodia's decentralisation framework.

participating-org.narrative:
The NGO Forum was started in Cambodia in the 1980s by international NGOs who wanted to put an end to Cambodia's international isolation and aid embargo. In the 1990s, as Cambodia opened up to the world, the NGO Forum became Cambodia-based, and began to invite local organisations to join as members. Nevertheless, it was still governed by an international Steering Committee and dominated by international NGOs right up to 1996. In 1997 a clear decision was made to make the NGO Forum more relevant to the concerns of the Cambodian people, resulting in an expansion of the membership base among local NGOs. A new expatriate representative was recruited and given the mandate to transition the NGO Forum towards full Cambodian leadership. Cambodian staff members began to play dominant roles in NGO Forum activities, and the first fully Cambodian Management Committee was elected in 2000. Over the course of the next eight years, the NGO Forum grew to respond to a number of emerging critical issues affecting poor and vulnerable communities across Cambodia.
The NGO Forum on Cambodia is a membership organisation for local and international NGOs based in Cambodia. It exists for the purpose of information sharing, debate and advocacy on priority issues affecting Cambodia's development. It aims to represent the viewsof the NGO community to decision-makers on issues such as development policy (overall economic and political issues), gender mainstreaming, and environmental protection and land rights. Presently the NGO Forum on Cambodia registers 79 full members and two associate members. Of the 79 full members, 46 are local NGOs and 33 are international NGOs.
